content:
The love of God is the greatest of all goods. It is the end for which we were created, the source of all true happiness, and the bond that unites the soul to its Creator. Without this love, all other virtues are dead; with it, even the smallest acts become precious in the sight of God.

Love is not a mere feeling. It is an act of the will by which we prefer God above all things and desire to do His will in everything. It is shown more by deeds than by words. He who truly loves God keeps His commandments, not out of fear of punishment, but out of desire to please the Beloved.

To grow in this love, we must often consider the goodness of God, the benefits He has given us, and above all the love He has shown us in the Passion of Jesus Christ. Frequent meditation on the Cross inflames the heart. Mental prayer, the sacraments, and acts of charity toward our neighbor are the ordinary means by which this love is increased.

Those who love God find peace even in suffering, because they know that every cross comes from the hand of a Father who loves them. They fear nothing except to offend Him. This is the love that makes saints.
